name: Loaded Mexican Potato Salad

ingredients.name: dried puya chiles, seeded and stemmed
dried chiles de árbol, seeded and stemmed
russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch chunks
kosher salt, plus more to taste
serrano chiles, stemmed and finely chopped

instructions.primary_message: Add 3 quarts water, puyas, and chiles de árbol to a large pot. Bring to a boil over high heat. Once water is boiling, transfer chiles and 1/2 cup cooking water to a blender. Set aside. Add potatoes and 2 tablespoons kosher salt to remaining water in large pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife, about 8 minutes.
Drain potatoes and arrange in an even layer on a rimmed baking sheet. Allow to cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, adjust oven rack to upper-middle position and preheat oven broiler to high. Arrange garlic on an aluminum foil-lined baking sheet and broil, flipping halfway through, until well charred, 5 to 8 minutes. Transfer to blender with chiles and water. Blend on high speed until smooth, about 1 minute. Season with salt to taste; set aside.

Reserve 2 teaspoons of the serranos, crumbled cotija, onion, and cilantro in a small bowl for garnish. In a large bowl, combine blended chile-garlic sauce, crema, mayonnaise, and cabbage. Add the remaining serranos, cotija, onion, and cilantro an stir with a spatula to combine. Fold in potatoes. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Top with reserved garnish. Refrigerate, covered, for at least 30 minutes or up to 4 days before serving. Serve with tostadas.

schema_metadata.keywords: potato salad recipe, mexican potato salad, flautas

description: This loaded Mexican potato salad transforms the classic flavors of flautas into a creamy, flavor-packed side dish with charred chile dressing, cotija, cabbage, and serranos.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 55 min.

Optional or for serving: Tostadas, for serving

Notes: If you can’t find puya chiles, you can use 1 to 2 guajillo chiles instead.
author: Octavio Peña
